title: How to Storm-Proof Your Exterior Paint for Gulf Coast Weather
description: Paint can't stop a hurricane, but the right prep, caulk, products and colors help your exterior shed wind-driven rain, resist UV and avoid moisture damage. Here's what holds up best in the Houston area.
author: Chris Petkau
content:
Short answer: no paint makes a house hurricane-proof, but a well-prepped, well-sealed exterior keeps wind-driven rain out of your walls. On the Gulf Coast, that means sealing every gap with quality caulk, priming bare wood, and using a 100% acrylic exterior paint with good UV and mildew resistance. A satin or low-sheen finish and lighter colors help too. The prep before the paint matters as much as the paint itself.

What Storm Season Does to Exterior Paint

  • Wind-driven rain gets pushed sideways into cracks, open joints and failed caulk that normal rain never reaches

  • Moisture behind the paint leads to blistering, peeling, wood rot and mildew

  • UV and heat the rest of the year break down paint and caulk, leaving gaps before the next storm

  • Flying debris chips paint and exposes bare wood or siding

Five Ways to Make Your Exterior Paint Storm-Ready

1. Seal every gap

Re-caulk around windows, doors, trim, siding joints and penetrations with a flexible, paintable exterior sealant. Failed caulk is the most common way water gets behind paint.

2. Fix and prime bare and damaged areas

Replace rotted wood, fill cracks in stucco with flexible patch, and prime any bare wood or new repairs before painting. Paint over an unsealed surface doesn't protect it.

3. Use a 100% acrylic exterior paint

Quality acrylic exterior paints stay flexible through heat and cold, resist mildew and hold up to UV. Elastomeric coatings can bridge hairline cracks on stucco and masonry, but they're not right for every surface. Ask before using them on wood siding.

4. Choose a satin or low-sheen finish

A little sheen sheds water and dirt better than flat paint while still hiding surface texture.

5. Lean toward lighter colors

Lighter colors absorb less heat, so the paint and the surface underneath expand and contract less, and they fade less in our sun. If you have vinyl siding, use a vinyl-safe color so the siding doesn't warp. See exterior colors that won't fade in Texas heat.

When to Schedule Exterior Work Around Storm Season

Atlantic hurricane season runs June 1 through November 30. Ideally, have your exterior inspected and repainted in spring, before the peak of the season, or in the fall once it winds down. If a storm has already damaged your paint or siding, see our guide to storm and water damage, from cleanup to fresh paint, and read about the best time to paint an exterior in Houston.

A Quick Pre-Season Checklist

  • Look for cracked, gapped or missing caulk around windows and doors

  • Check trim and fascia for soft or rotted wood

  • Look for peeling, blistering or chalky paint

  • Check stucco and brick for cracks

  • Clear gutters so water doesn't overflow onto siding

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the best exterior paint for the Houston climate?

A premium 100% acrylic exterior paint with UV and mildew resistance, applied over proper prep. See our top picks for Texas homes.

Can paint really protect a house from storms?

Paint and caulk are the outer seal of your walls. They won't stop structural damage, but they keep everyday wind-driven rain out, which prevents rot and mildew.

How often should a Houston-area exterior be repainted?

It depends on the surface, sun exposure and the quality of the last job. Check yours yearly and repaint when caulk fails or paint starts to chalk, crack or peel.
